tasks.short: Measure workplace noise and conduct hearing conservation programmes

steps.what: Measure noise levels and assess workplace exposure conditions
Conduct hearing conservation programs with workplace participants

tasks.design: Keep workplace measurement, exposure interpretation and programme delivery with the audiologist. Use {DOCS} to retain measurement context and programme decisions without introducing a model or assuming an automated safety conclusion.
tasks.previous_blocker: Noise exposure depends on where, when and how work is performed.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing measurement instruments and documents support the current process.
tasks.still_hard: Representative sampling and practical changes to noisy working conditions.
tasks.human_edge: The audiologist relates observations to actual work and coaches participants.

reach.learn: Match sampling conditions to real work patterns

evidence.claim: The supplied digest establishes no measured automation of workplace hearing conservation; this manual design is an E1 proposal.

assumptions: The task baseline consists of measurement, assessment and programme delivery rather than report transcription.
The audiologist produces noise readings, measurement context and the exposure assessment in s1; all capture and interpretation time remains counted.
Existing measurement tools and DOCS suffice; no custom safety decision service is built.
No new workflow means zero incremental upkeep; existing calibration work remains within current measurement practice.
research_questions: Is there repeated transcription distinct from the field measurement and programme delivery baseline?

already_counted.description: Measurement capture, exposure assessment and programme delivery

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100; gross and net saving zero. Instrument readings do not replace representative sampling or programme delivery.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop and supervise hearing screening programmes

steps.what: Develop hearing screening programs and define clinical follow-up arrangements
Supervise screening practice and resolve programme quality concerns

tasks.design: Retain programme design and clinical supervision with the audiologist, recording decisions in {DOCS}. Scheduling and individual record preparation are separate activities and provide no saving in this task.
tasks.previous_blocker: A suitable screening programme needs clinical judgment and a functioning follow-up pathway.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing planning documents support accountable programme development.
tasks.still_hard: Balancing population coverage, test limitations and follow-up capacity.
tasks.human_edge: The audiologist identifies poor practice and makes defensible changes.

reach.learn: Assess reach and completion of follow-up pathways

evidence.claim: Programme development and supervision remain manual in this proposed design; no hearing-screening management saving is established by the digest.

assumptions: Developing and supervising programmes excludes administering each screening test and writing each patient note.

Screening staff produce observations and outcomes while delivering separate screening encounters; this design adds no structured intake requirement. The audiologist reviews their context within s2 with full time retained.
Use existing DOCS before introducing a workflow platform.
No new automated rules or service require incremental upkeep.
research_questions: Which programme decisions currently lack sufficient follow-up evidence?

already_counted.description: Programme design, evidence review and supervision

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100 gives zero gross and net saving. Administrative savings from other tasks are excluded.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Responsible hearing conservation and screening oversight
reach: Coordinate with occupational safety specialists on representative measurements
Work with public health practitioners on follow-up capacity
role.ambitious_version: An audiologist who improves programme quality through direct observation and clear clinical responsibility
